To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the biodiversity of life on Earth has evolved over the past half billion years, that the diversity of life on Earth is not evenly distributed across space or time, and that the diversity of species is not evenly distributed among the major groups of organisms.

(1) the scientific basis for biodiversity inventories is systematics, (2) the goal of systematics is the discovery of evolutionary patterns and processes, (3) the goal of biodiversity inventories is to provide data for the discovery of evolutionary pattern and process, (4) the scientific basis of systematics and biodiversity inventories is comparative morphology, and (5) the scientific basis is the foundation for biodiversity inventories.

(1) the biodiversity crisis can be met with a comprehensive taxonomic inventory strategy; (2) the taxonomic inventory strategy proposed here can be used for all taxa; (3) taxonomic inventory strategies are compatible with the needs of basic research; (4) taxonomic inventory data can be used for the study of the origin and history life; and (5) taxonomic inventory results can be used to inform decisions about conservation and resource management.
In summary, our research is concerned with
documenting and understanding biodiversity.
the discovery and description of biodiversity and its patterns of distribution.
the discovery, description, and classification of organisms.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
taxonomic inventories of biodiversity are essential for the advancement of science, for the management of natural resources, and for conservation of the world's biodiversity.
inventories are essential to the future of biodiversity science.
taxonomic inventories provide the foundation for all biodiversity studies, including conservation, resource management, and basic biological research.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have made a significant contribution to the scientific community by producing a taxonomic inventory strategy for the exploration of biological diversity on Earth and beyond.
the inventory strategy we propose is an effective way to meet the goals of biodiversity exploration.
we are in the business of providing data for the science of systematics, the scientific foundation of biodiversity inventories.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a systematic approach to inventory is the most efficient and effective way to gather information on biodiversity, and that the information is most useful when it is associated with voucher specimens that are stored in museums and herbaria.
the biodiversity crisis can be addressed by a concerted effort to collect, describe, and archive the world’s biota.

the taxonomic inventory strategy we propose is the only one that will provide the data needed for understanding the origin of biological diversity and for making informed decisions about conservation and resource management.
